what_it_does: Designing a modern high-performance processor chip involves choosing among billions of possible combinations of design parameters (cache sizes, pipeline depths, memory bandwidth, and so on), and simulating each option is slow and expensive. This paper presents SEBO, a smarter search strategy based on Bayesian optimization — a technique that builds a statistical model of which designs are likely to be good, then uses that model to decide which options are worth simulating next, rather than trying them at random. SEBO specifically improves three parts of that search: how it picks the first batch of designs to try, how it builds its statistical model, and how it decides which design to try next. The goal is to find chip configurations that are best on multiple objectives at once — power, performance, and silicon area — with far fewer expensive simulations, demonstrated on a real Arm server processor design.
